title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 277
paragraphs: At the times when they gather at the city of Saïs for their sacrifices, on a certain night they all kindle lamps in great numbers in the open air around their houses. The lamps are saucers full of salt and oil mixed, with the wick floating by itself on the surface, and this burns throughout the whole night; and to the festival is given the name Lychnocaia (the Lighting of the Lamps). Moreover, those Egyptians who have not come to this solemn assembly observe the night of the festival and themselves also light lamps — all of them — so that lamps are lit not in Saïs alone but over all Egypt. As to why light and honour are allotted to this night, a sacred story is told about it.
